question: Tell me about a time your team was moving without thinking and producing useless work. How did you get them to add just enough planning?

raiseTranscript.text: On my first project I was building a reporting script that kept crashing on edge cases. The team was pushing to ship daily without checking data quality, so we generated 200 useless reports.
I added a 15-minute data validation step in the morning standup and showed one example of bad output. It slowed us by half a day total but cut rework by 80%.
They were annoyed at first but after seeing the fixed output they asked me to own the check going forward.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time your team was moving without thinking and producing useless work. How did you get them to add just enough planning?
Role: new grad on first project, individual contributor
Situation: daily script runs producing bad reports due to no validation
Action: proposed 15-min data check in standup and showed one bad example
Outcome: rework dropped 80%, team adopted the step
Quote: 'They asked me to own the check going forward'
Follow-up: How did the team react? -> They were annoyed at first but then requested ownership
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar on Bias for Action for a junior. The candidate spotted local useless output and inserted a minimal planning step without stopping the team. Quote shows they used one concrete example rather than a long meeting. This demonstrates ownership of their own work and quick learning from visible failure. The outcome stayed within individual scope yet influenced the immediate workflow. Biggest strength is turning personal frustration into a repeatable check the team kept.

lowerTranscript.text: We were building features fast and some turned out not to be used.
What did you do about it?
I kept coding what the PM asked and waited for the next sprint to drop the unused ones.

raiseTranscript.text: Two teams were building duplicate analytics pipelines because each moved fast on their own OKRs.
I pulled the two tech leads into a 30-minute mapping session, documented the overlap, and got them to agree on a shared weekly sync instead of a full design doc.
Duplicate work stopped within two weeks and both teams reused one pipeline; the sync became the only new process.

raiseTranscript.text: Three product lines were each funding separate data platforms that overlapped 70%.
I ran a two-week discovery with the three GMs, surfaced the overlap cost in headcount, and mandated a single platform team with a lightweight quarterly review instead of new roadmaps.
Platform spend dropped 25% in the next fiscal year and the review became the only recurring planning touchpoint.
